newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks down as foreign funds stay away.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks down as foreign funds stay away.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended down in busy trading marked by the absence of foreign funds.
Bogota's IBB index dipped 0.57 percent to 1,072.66 on volume of 5.6 billion pesos, while Medellin's IBOMED index dropped 0.63 percent to 16,594.5 on one billion pesos.
About half the volume in Bogota was made up of a cross deal in finance company Crecer SA at an unchanged price of 485 pesos.

"Foreign funds want to see big packets of good stocks that nobody can offer at the moment and domestic investors seem as if they want to wait until after Easter Week before they invest, so the trend is downward," one Bogota trader said.
One of the biggest falls was Bancoquia bank, down 4.84 percent to 3,202 in Bogota and down 0.33 percent to 3,339 in Medellin.
Cementos del Caribe dipped 3.67 percent to 5,298 in Bogota and 1.85 percent to 5,300 in Medellin. Brewer Bavaria was down 1.41 percent at 6,980 in Bogota and 1.13 percent at 7,000 in Medellin.

Banco de Colombia fell 0.93 percent to 424 pesos in Bogota and 1.17 percent to the same price in Medellin. The fall came despite reports in local media that Spain's Banco Central Hispano had tied up a deal to buy a 25 percent stake in the Colombian bank for $120 million.

"There's a lot of disinformation and nobody has come out and officially said the deal is wrapped up and that worries investors," another Bogota broker said. Greater falls in Tuesday's sessions were offset by a 2.22 percent rise in Suramericana de Seguros CS.ML in Bogota to 23,000 and a 1.93 percent rise to the same price in Medellin.
